device_measured_reason: No physical device runtime was authorized for this lane (§6). All client durations are PENDING_RUNTIME.

headline_finding.statement: The iOS and Android Scanner client paths are the SAME CODE. There is not one Platform.OS or Platform.select branch anywhere in hooks/useKScan.js, services/imageUtils.js, services/scanIdentification.ts, services/scannerScanRequest.ts, services/scannerEvidenceGateway.ts or components/scan-room/.
headline_finding.consequence: Any iOS/Android performance difference on this path originates inside the native implementations of expo-camera and expo-image-manipulator, not in K Scan's own logic. That is a DEVICE-MEASURED question this lane cannot answer and must not guess.

capture_api.note: No base64 flag, no exif flag, no skipProcessing — the call returns a file URI only, so nothing is encoded at shutter time.

gallery_api.value: ImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAsync({ mediaTypes: ['images'], quality: 1, allowsEditing: false, allowsMultipleSelection: false })
gallery_api.note: allowsMultipleSelection:false — single image per session. quality:1 means the gallery path hands compressForUpload an uncompressed-as-picked source.

resize.hazard: Width-only resize sets the width EXACTLY, so a source narrower than 896 px is UPSCALED. Verified against the committed corpus: 5 of the 8 assets/qa_fixtures images upscale, dress.jpg by 4.49x in pixel count. This costs encoded bytes and upload time for zero added detail, and it bites the GALLERY/upload entry path (small or screenshot sources), not the camera path.

encoding.value: base64: true, then wrapped as `data:image/jpeg;base64,${result.base64}` and stripped back to raw base64 before send

rotation_exif_metadata.value: No explicit rotation step and no EXIF option anywhere on the path. The JPEG re-encode drops EXIF implicitly, which the V2 contract declares honestly as rawExifTransmitted:false.

privacy_processing.value: NONE. sanitizeImageBeforeUpload is a proven passthrough (`return input`), with faceDetectionAvailable:false and plateMaskApplied:false. localPrivacyFiltered is therefore always false on the wire.

transport.value: supabase.functions.invoke('scan-identify', { body, signal }) — a JSON document with the base64 image inside it. NOT multipart, NOT a binary body, NOT a storage upload followed by a URL.

client_size_cap.source: services/scanIdentification.ts:37 MAX_IMAGE_BASE64_BYTES, enforced at :482-484 before any network call
client_size_cap.server_side_equivalent: index.ts:180 MAX_IMAGE_BASE64_BYTES = 2*1024*1024, enforced independently of the client

modeled_capture_geometry.note: MODELED, not measured. Used only to compute payload sizes; the post-resize width is PROVEN to be 896 regardless.

modeled_bytes_per_pixel_at_quality_065.derivation: OBSERVED bytes-per-pixel range of the 8 committed assets/qa_fixtures JPEGs, computed from real file bytes and real SOF dimensions: min 0.0563, median 0.2387, max 0.3766. Those fixtures are at unknown encoder qualities, so the mapping to quality 0.65 specifically is MODELED. Real post-compression bytes are PENDING_RUNTIME.
